pr_title: Pop expired watchers in case there is no update to cache
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As reported over #80690, when there is no service update, we should still pop expired watcher(s) to prevent leak.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #80690

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs

```

Added new test for the scenario.
```
			if len(cacher.bookmarkWatchers.watchersBuckets) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("unexpected bookmark watchers %v", len(cacher.bookmarkWatchers.watchersBuckets))
			}
```
Without the fix, the above check would fail.

I added mutex due to the data race reported below:
```
Read at 0x00c00015a420 by goroutine 69:

      staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go:788 +0x386

Previous write at 0x00c00015a420 by goroutine 67:
  runtime.mapassign_fast64()
      GOROOT/src/runtime/map_fast64.go:92 +0x0
  k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher.(*watcherBookmarkTimeBuckets).addWatcher()
      staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go:193 +0x21e
  k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher.(*Cacher).Watch.func1()
      staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go:509 +0x343
  k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher.(*Cacher).Watch()
      staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go:512 +0x7e7
  k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher.TestCacherNoLeakWhenNoUpdate()
      staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher_whitebox_test.go:605 +0x310

```
Since the watcher addition is not frequent, I expect not much impact on performance.

> Since the watcher addition is not frequent, I expect not much impact on performance.

Lock is required. I have met some panic of concurrent map read and map write here in our environment.

issue_context.title: apiserver leaks memory cause by bookmark
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I try to backport bookmark feature to our internal branch. When I enable bookmark feature, apiserver leaks memory. I spend some time to dig the root cause and find the bookmarkWatchers of service cacher is keep increasing. I am not sure if it exists at upstream code. Please let me know if it is ok at latest code.

**What you expected to happen**:
Avoid memory leaking

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Run a cluster.
2. Do not update service.
3. You will find kube-apiserver's memory keep increasing.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Kubelet will watch service with bookmark, and add a watcher to bookmarkWatchers.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/23649560c060ad6cd82da8da42302f8f7e38cf1e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L508-L510

and service init resource version is 0
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/23649560c060ad6cd82da8da42302f8f7e38cf1e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L773

Without updating service, we cannot update "lastProcessedResourceVersion", it will keep 0,  bookmarkTimer branch will always be continued.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/23649560c060ad6cd82da8da42302f8f7e38cf1e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L774-L802

As a result, it cannot trigger popExpiredWatchers, so the service watcher will keep increasing every watching.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/23649560c060ad6cd82da8da42302f8f7e38cf1e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L197

comments: @hormes - can you also please take a look?

@tedyu Agree with u. That's same way I fix in our branch.
But I wanna hear the suggestion of @wojtek-t and @hormes .

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10073361/62018263-957e6e80-b1ec-11e9-8a33-4519b0fe8a15.png)
With the same bugfix @tedyu wrote above, we can see the memory not increasing any more.

Given that watch-bookmarks doesn't create any additional go-routines (well, creates 1, but cannot leak them), it has to leak the data. The only data that can be leaked is exactly bookmarkWatchers.

So I looked into the code and got into exactly the same conclusion - that we must be leaking watchers for resources that aren't changing.

The fix as above makes sense (though we also need a unit test for it).

Thanks for reporting the bug, I will look at #80692 this day later.

In addition, also need to think carefully about whether need to send a bookmark when there are no events at all. @wojtek-t

review_comments: As comments above, this structure is not thread-safe. Watchers and bookmark buckets are synchronized by mutex in Cacher, can we keep this pattern with current implementation?

1. With this test, the keeping the previous one doesn't make sense imho.

2. Did you check that this test is really catching the problem - it's not actually that obvious to me.
[I think that with 10 watchers, it actually may not really be failing.]
The way to check that would be to temporary move the lock to where it was before and run this test and this test should fail.

@wojtek-t 
I removed the first test since there is significant overlap between the two.

I increased number of watchers to 20.

w.r.t. triggering the race condition, the following has to be satisfied:

1. addWatcher runs and obtains bucketID but hasn't taken the lock
2. popExpiredWatchers runs, takes the lock and processes the watchers at position t.startBucketID
3. before addWatcher gets a chance to resume, popExpiredWatchers advances t.startBucketID
4. addWatcher resumes with bucketID lower than t.startBucketID - leading to leak

Note that both func's use t.clock.Now() at the beginning.
However, addWatcher doesn't take the lock even though it runs prior to popExpiredWatchers.

With instrumentation, it would be easier to show this race condition but I don't think that's what we should do.

I wasn't asking what has to happen to trigger a race.
And I don't want to you to instrument the code.

I want to see that it was failing before.

I guess what Jordan and myself are trying to say is that if you have a test that is not failing even with the race that Jordan found in majority of cases, we will most probably not catch the regression if we regress again in the future (and that is exactly the point of having this test).
I did not understand the purpose of this case, sorry for that. I think we need a case which runs dispatchEvents and Watch, and verify the watcher is leaked after that.
Wrap this line with c.Lock() c.Unlock()

bookmarkWatchers struct is NOT thread-safe.
I think we should lock here.
do we also need to pop expired bookmark watchers on the other handler paths that return (line 783 and 807)?
by only removing expired watchers when there's no resource change, does that mean a constantly changing resource (like endpoints) would still effectively leak?
how expensive is popExpiredWatchers to call? is it concerning to call it approximately once a second?

> do we also need to pop expired bookmark watchers on the other handler paths that return (line 783 and 807)?

I don't think so - those effectively can happen only when we're closing cacher.

> by only removing expired watchers when there's no resource change, does that mean a constantly changing resource (like endpoints) would still effectively leak?

not sure I understand your question - can you please clarify?

> how expensive is popExpiredWatchers to call? is it concerning to call it approximately once a second?

cheap enough - we're calling it every 1s anyway as part of dispatchEvent call (somewhere down the stack)

For the two places Jordan mentioned, c.dispatchEvent would handle expired watchers (via startDispatching).
So there is no source for leak after this fix goes in.

I also thought about whether the expired bookmark watchers need to be popped for every period in case there is no update.
We can use a counter - beyond a threshold, say 5, we pop the watchers.

I am open to suggestion in this regard.

>> by only removing expired watchers when there's no resource change, does that mean a constantly changing resource (like endpoints) would still effectively leak?
>
> not sure I understand your question - can you please clarify?

I misread the code... this is skipping pruning expired watchers if this cacher has **never** received a watch event for the resource type. Same question exists, but in the opposite direction now. ~~By only removing expired watchers when there's a resource change, does that mean an almost never-changing resource (like APIService) would still effectively leak?~~

edit: finished reading the dispatchEvent() code, and see that popExpiredWatchers is called when handling the sent bookmark event

Jordan:
I see you modified previous comment
Do you have any more question ?
